appearance_bounds.source_title: Fifth census of the United States, 1830 — the division headed 'Peoria & Putnam Counties & Territory attached'
appearance_bounds.identity_rule: Surname and given name both agree between the 1830 reading 'John K Clark' and the town person 'John A Clark' in household hh_clark_john_a. The 1830 line is carried as EARLIER EVIDENCE for that person and grades nothing on its own.
appearance_bounds.note: A BOUND ON PRESENCE IN A DISTRICT, AND NOT AT CHICAGO. The division is headed 'Peoria & Putnam Counties & Territory attached' and the schedule never writes the word Chicago — the Fox River and Du Page settlements are inside it — so this row bounds presence in that district in the summer of 1830 and puts no body in the town, which is why `here_by` is null. The record's own note says it first: 'Presence in that district in the summer of 1830; not a Chicago residence, and never an 1835 one'. Under the evidence ladder ratified 2026-09-03 a source EARLIER than the scene date corroborates and dates and never promotes, and a source LATER than it does not promote either. THE IDENTITY IS INFERRED AND THE PAGE IS NOT: the leaf is read scan_verified off the federal schedule, and what no source states is that the head of family on it is the person on this card. data/research/census_1830/resident_crosswalk.json joins them on a name agreement and says in terms that it grades nothing on its own. No grade moves here and the identity is neither reopened nor hardened.

merge_ruling.for_merge: 'Chark' is one letter from Clark, h for l, and the forename 'John A.' agrees letter for letter with John A. Clark, in the Democrat of 11 February 1834 (#c001) — the same middle initial A. The stem 'Chark' is set nowhere in the deposited corpus and the town holds no other bearer of it: on the face of it a card minted off a garble.
merge_ruling.against_merge: A GARBLED READING CANNOT BE TESTED, AND THERE ARE TWO CLARKS IT COULD BE. R5 is the standing refusal and T-0695 is the ticket that reads these cards at the image; T-1027 files `chark_john_a` under the garbles in its own words — 'a fold here would repair a wreck by guessing at it'. The guess is not even single-valued: the town holds clark_john_a and clark_john_k, and the `clark-john` cluster has already ruled those two DISTINCT under D1 on their contradicting middle initials, so a fold of 'John A. Chark' would have to choose which of two ruled-apart men to join. Clark is set 2,655 times in the corpus and the reading index holds 37 Clark identities. R5, and the reading belongs to T-0695.

Both cards print an explicit middle initial and the two disagree — A against K — with no anchor on either side to say one of them is mis-set. Two men until something says otherwise, and the ruling is written onto both cards so the next pass does not re-ask.

replaceable_by.match: a source that states this person's age, their birth year, or an interval either can be read out of

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('clark_john_a:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

sex_basis.note: A FORENAME THAT STANDS IN ONE SEX'S NAMING ONLY. 'John' is read as male because 14 persons in this layer whose sex a source records bear it (bates_john_jr, calhoun_john, caton_john_dean, davis_john, greene_john, hogan_john_s_c, and others), and it stands in the irish and yankee male forename pool of this town's own attested naming. Nothing about this person is recorded; the name is the whole of the reasoning, and the table that licenses it — data/research/residents/forename_sex.json — refuses a name its own evidence splits, refuses Jean, Marion, Leslie and Francis by name, and refuses an initial outright.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. WHAT THIS PASS RULED ONTO THIS HOUSEHOLD, named so the ruling can be found again: each volume below is followed by the printed entries it set against this person and the status the crosswalk ruled them at — a single entry carries what its own `could_carry` declares, and an ambiguous or contested match carries nothing and is shown so that the silence is legible. clark_john_a, Fergus's Chicago directory of 1839 — f1839_e0286 (contested, so nothing crossed); clark_john_a, the advertising cards in Norris's directory of 1844 — n1844_ad0020 (contested, so nothing crossed).
